exposure: Maternal micronutrient intake patterns and adherence
outcome: Prevalence and adherence patterns of micronutrient supplementation
Association with maternal characteristics (e.g., age, education, residence, pregnancy planning, parity, previous spontaneous abortion, antenatal care initiation)
Maternal and newborn obesogenic effect of supplementation
cohort: 300 pregnant women who delivered in a university hospital in Hungary.
finding: While prenatal micronutrient intake was common among Hungarian pregnant women, adherence to recommended levels was low, and supplementation with FA and O3 was associated with improved obstetric outcomes such as a lower likelihood of cesarean section, improved uterine contractility, and reduced risk of gestational diabetes mellitus.
mod_finding: Folic acid intake correlated with a lower likelihood of cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from pregnant women who delivered, using self-reported questionnaires and clinical records, likely covering the prenatal period at the time of delivery or shortly after.
